title: BRUCK SYNDROME 2
alt_titles: OSTEOGENESIS IMPERFECTA WITH CONGENITAL JOINT CONTRACTURES

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Bruck syndrome-2 (BRKS2) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the PLOD2 gene on chromosome 3q23-q24.

paragraphs.text: Bruck syndrome is an autosomal recessive disorder in which skeletal changes resembling osteogenesis imperfecta, including osteopenia, fragile bones and multiple fractures, occur together with congenital contractures of the large joints. Pterygia may be present at birth (Ha-Vinh et al., 2004). Bank et al. (1999) described Bruck syndrome as osteoporosis, joint contractures, fragile bones, and short stature. The biochemical defect is underhydroxylation of lysine residues in the telopeptides of type I collagen in bone, which leads to reduced pyridinoline crosslinks (Bank et al., 1999; van der Slot et al., 2003).

paragraphs.text: Bank et al. (1999) found that, in bone from patients with Bruck syndrome, lysine residues in the telopeptides of type I collagen were underhydroxylated, which led to aberrant crosslinking. Lysine residues in the triple helix were modified normally. Unlike bone, cartilage and ligament had normal telopeptide hydroxylation, as shown by normal crosslinking patterns. Bank et al. (1999) concluded that collagen crosslinking is regulated mainly by tissue-specific enzymes that hydroxylate only telopeptide lysine residues, and they proposed that a bone-specific telopeptide lysyl hydroxylase was defective in Bruck syndrome.

paragraphs.text: Puig-Hervás et al. (2012) studied 6 consanguineous families with Bruck syndrome. In 2 probands, they found a homozygous frameshift mutation (c.1559dupC) in the alternative exon 13a of the PLOD2 gene. This indicated that specific inactivation of the longer protein isoform encoded by PLOD2 is enough to cause Bruck syndrome. A homozygous c.1856G-A mutation in PLOD2, resulting in an arg619-to-his (R619H) substitution, was found in an Egyptian patient. In a patient with autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta, homozygosity mapping followed by a candidate gene approach identified a homozygous donor splice site mutation in PLOD2. Screening of further samples found compound heterozygous PLOD2 mutations, including a c.1864G-T change resulting in a gly622-to-cys (G622C) substitution, in 2 Spanish brothers. One brother had mild autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta and the other had mild Bruck syndrome. Puig-Hervás et al. (2012) concluded that PLOD2 mutations cause Bruck syndrome and are also associated with autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta of variable severity.

checks.evidence_quote: Row: Spain | 18 | Compound heterozygote | c.1864G>T, p.Gly622Cys | Puig-Hervas et al (2012) [*]
checks.explanation: Second-hand: the evidence is a table row of Patra et al. (2026) (PMID 42147077) describing PMID 22689593, not the paper's own text; the claim was not checked against PMID 22689593 itself. Verdict on the later paper's description: partially_supported. The G622C variant is not in the abstract and comes only from a citing paper's table.

checks.claim: Of 2 Spanish brothers with compound heterozygous PLOD2 mutations including G622C, one had mild Bruck syndrome-2 and the other had mild autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta.
checks.evidence_quote: compound heterozygous mutations in PLOD2 in two brothers, one affected with mild AR-OI and the other with mild BS
